claim.summary: Private and government slavery are well attested under the Western Han, but the evidence does not support treating slave labour as a dominant industrial or agricultural system. Earlier scholarship describes marked growth in private and government slavery, while recent work argues that fiscal and labour-market changes produced very low levels of slave ownership in the mature Han private economy.

territorial_practice.notes: P2 records repeated and institutionally recognized slavery while preserving the specialist finding that mature Han slave ownership was low and large-scale private slave labour was discouraged.

source.title: Industrial Slavery in China During the Former Han Dynasty (206 B.C.–A.D. 25)
source.independence_notes: Classic dedicated study of Former Han slavery.
source.reliability_limitations: Originally published in 1943; interpretation must be balanced against more recent scholarship.
